The derivation incorporates weights computed from equation (3.2), for which hat(w_j)=w_j angle-2n_j. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed quotient.)

The relative forward error and cond(x,n,f) require p_n(x) != 0, inherited from Definition 2.1 and also forced by the denominator |p_n(x)| in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
implicit_context: p_n(x) is the exact interpolated value for the given inputs, whereas hat(p_n(x)) is the result of floating-point evaluation including computed-weight errors. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: computed expression.)

The exact finite counter representation precedes and supports the first-order expansion in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression; PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)

The first condition-number term measures sensitivity to f, while the second term measures cancellation in the formula's denominator and is independent of f. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: paragraph following Theorem 4.1.)
The theorem inherits fixed interpolation points and fixed x from Section 2; it is not a bound for perturbations of those quantities. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
norms: The theorem uses scalar absolute values; each numerator of a condition quotient is a sum of termwise absolute values, and each denominator is the absolute value of the corresponding exact sum. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
No vector or function norm appears in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
numerical_model: The model is fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta)^(+1 or -1), |delta| <= u, for op in {+,-,*,/}, with u the unit roundoff. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: standard floating-point model.)
The inputs x_i, f_i, and x are assumed already to be floating-point numbers. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: paragraph immediately before Lemma 3.1.)

Computed weights contribute angle-2n_j; after all numerator operations and the final quotient error are collected, numerator terms carry angle-(3n+4)_j, while denominator terms carry angle-(3n+2)_j. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: Lemma 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)
The counters are deterministic bounded relative errors; the paper does not impose probabilistic independence. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, anchor: equation (3.3) and subscript-j convention.)

undebatable_constraints: The algorithm is the second/proper barycentric quotient (4.1), not the first/modified Lagrange formula. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: equation (4.1).)

The exact finite model must preserve separate perturbed numerator and denominator sums, with collected counters 3n+4 and 3n+2 respectively. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 551, anchor: exact computed expression.)
The forward bound has two additive first-order terms, not just cond(x,n,f)u. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1.)
The first coefficient is (3n+4)u and the second is (3n+2)u. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equations (4.2)-(4.3).)
The second condition number is cond(x,n,1), where 1 is the constant-one function/data. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: equation (4.3) and following sentence.)
The O(u^2) term may not be silently dropped when reproducing Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.2)-(4.3).)
The theorem's error is relative forward error against the exact p_n(x), so p_n(x) must be nonzero. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
The paper additionally claims existential sharpness within a constant factor. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 552, anchor: sentence following equation (4.3).)
